mstts:express-as.prosody: Have you ever wondered if everything we think we know about raising kids might actually be a little off? It turns out, beneath all the familiar advice about parenting, there are some truly eye-opening truths just waiting to be discovered. Together, we're about to dig into NurtureShock: New Thinking About Children, written by Po Bronson. This isn’t just another parenting book—it’s a journey that challenges what we take for granted. With every page, Bronson invites us to question the usual rules and look at raising children through the lens of fascinating science. Imagine finding out that the way we praise our kids could actually be working against them, or that sleep plays a far bigger role in their growth than we ever realized. What if the things we think are harmless—like a little white lie—are actually more complicated? As we explore these discoveries together, we’ll uncover insights that might just change how we see childhood itself. You and I are going to peel back the layers of those old parenting myths. We’ll get a closer look at the real effects of sibling rivalry, how kids come to understand race, what self-control truly means, and why intelligence isn’t as straightforward as we once believed. Each new finding isn’t just surprising—it’s empowering. So, if you’re ready to rethink what it means to nurture, guide, and really understand the children in your life, you’re in the right place. Let’s start this journey together, and see how a little curiosity—and a lot of science—can reshape what we thought we knew about raising the next generation.
